title: CLAUDE.md
text: Abundance always TotalAreaMS1 / TotalIonCurrentArea (TIC-normalised). Raw area never used thresholding. RiskLevel ordered integer factor 0–6 maps human-readable labels (“0) Detected” … “5) High”, “6) threshold reference”). integer used colour-scaling; label display. summarize_conta() uses ... (dot-dot-dot) accept arbitrary grouping variables, making reusable across contaminant, sample, condition, dataset-level summaries. Rmd template embeds print_plot_or_plotly() — local wrapper — toggle static (ggplot2) interactive (plotly) output via params$PlotsInteractive. Thresholds sourced reference run quantiles reference set; none provided, get_simple_thresholds_*() sets uniform arbitrary thresholds warns user.

title: Getting started with HowDirty
text: Two files required: 1. Skyline peak-area export — CSV produced Skyline’s File → Export → Report dialog using contaminant report definition. file must contain columns protein (contaminant name), peptide, replicate name, retention time, total MS1 area, total ion current area. 2. title: Evaluate How Dirty are LC-MS Samples
text: HowDirty R package assesses level contamination LC-MS results. presence contaminants (e.g., PEG), detergents (e.g., CHAPS, SDS) samples analyzed LC-MS can severely detrimental identifying peptides/proteins molecules. Skyline used extra MS1 features many known contaminant masses raw files (e.g., .raw .d). results exported .csv file, processed R using HowDirty generate HTML interactive report evaluates sample contamination risks. details, please see publication tutorial ().
